newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crude rises late, ANS diff narrows.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crude rises late, ANS diff narrows.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crudes continued rising late Wednesday, driven by speculative buying in the West Texas Intermediate (WTI) aftermarket and narrowing discounts for Alaskan crude.

Discounts for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude tightened seven cents from Tuesday to $1.75 below WTI, as a West Coast refiner bought its second full cargo of ANS in two days and put the number of fixed deals done this week at three.
With index WTI rising 20 cents a barrel over late Tuesday levels, ANS firmed to $23.15/23.35 a barrel, or 33 cents over yesterday.
Diffs for Line 63, remained unchanged at $3.20/3.00 under WTI.
No deals were rumored for California heavy crudes, which remain abundant amid refiner problems and trimmed output in response to weak West Coast margins.
Prices were stable for heavies after rising Monday on increased posted prices.
